_about: Our combined lessons: what we learned building this app together. enforced_by / checked_by use kind prefixes (py:, setting:, file:, rule:); arch_lessons.check() verifies every target exists. trains_via = the curriculum family or tag that teaches it (null = none yet). Shown as a table in docs/PRINCIPLES.md.

lessons.lesson: Keep the worker fully on the card and the mixture-of-experts heavy model beside it; never let a second model take layers from the worker, and never plan on an idle GPU.
lessons.evidence: Worker speed 7.96 -> 70.9 tok/s once Ollama stopped putting the heavy MoE on the card and the worker got all its layers; heavy beside the worker 14-16 tok/s with ~1 s switching.

lessons.lesson: A test or tool never touches the real settings file: every suite runs in a throwaway ARCHITECT_HOME and ARCHITECT_DATA_DIR.
lessons.evidence: Two suites wiped architect_config.json (the config-wipe incident); since then every runner builds a fresh home per suite.

lessons.lesson: Small models fail on wiring, not logic: code fixes exports, __main__ and __init__; the model writes the logic.
lessons.evidence: 26 of 153 failed live builds failed on the contract's shape (function never exported, CLI without __main__.py, package without __init__.py); about half of failed whole-project builds in a 30-build run.

lessons.lesson: State every public name and its arguments before any sprint writes code; the request's own contract wins over the planner's.
lessons.evidence: Whole-file rewrites silently dropped functions an earlier sprint built; the interface block in every sprint prompt and DEF blocks stopped it.

lessons.lesson: A retry needs only the failing assertion and the code it exercises, not the whole history (error-driven repair).
lessons.evidence: Recorded as a rule from live builds; the harness trims failure logs and the fix prompt names the failing assertion. No separate measurement yet.

lessons.lesson: Tests a model writes for its own code miss the edges; hidden acceptance tests judge builds, not the model's own.
lessons.evidence: No number yet: the e2e family judges whole builds by hidden tests with a reference and a deliberately wrong solution. Training tagged edge_cases is planned.

lessons.lesson: After any fan-out that writes, a read-only verifier tries to prove it wrong; a workflow that can write must end with one.
lessons.evidence: Verifiers caught a symlink / zip-slip hole, telemetry that could leak secrets, and a stale resume that replayed old results.

lessons.lesson: Later phases get a short digest of earlier results, not their transcripts; every agent's prompt starts with one shared, byte-identical, cacheable header.
lessons.evidence: Claude lead: 98% prompt-cache hit with the shared header. Local fake run: an 8-finding result of ~5,000 characters reaches the next phase as <=800.

lessons.lesson: Report every rate with its interval; a small sample does not rank models.
lessons.evidence: 7 of 16 passed is 44%, but the 95% interval is 23-67%: two such runs cannot be told apart.

lessons.lesson: Compare changes with line endings ignored, or churn hides the real diff.
lessons.evidence: The same change measured 23k changed lines with CRLF/LF churn and 2.2k without.

lessons.lesson: One file owner per agent; two running agents never share a file or a folder and a file in it; no git stash, checkout or reset in a shared tree.
lessons.evidence: Ownership is now refused before anything runs (OwnershipClash); a git stash in a shared tree would hide another agent's uncommitted work.

lessons.lesson: Size context by role: planner prompts 12k -> 8k, router 8k -> 4k (then 2k in the shipped profile); a crew agent never sees more than half its role's window of earlier results.
lessons.evidence: Windows were cut 12k -> 8k (planner) and 8k -> 4k (router); the router's window must never size project context.

lessons.lesson: A Qwen3 draft cannot speed Qwen3.5/3.6: a draft needs the worker's exact tokenizer.
lessons.evidence: Draft needs the worker's exact tokenizer (pick_draft checks it); n-gram speculation (edits 56 -> 306-343 tok/s) stayed the default.

lessons.lesson: Writing tests first did not help small models; do not add it as a default step.
lessons.evidence: No gain at n=16 (interval too wide to claim any effect).

lessons.lesson: Claude-written text may feed retrieval, playbooks and statistics, never fine-tuning.
lessons.evidence: Rule from the Claude tools build: runs with a claude transport or claude: model are excluded from every dataset export.

lessons.lesson: The server can only reuse a prompt start that is byte-identical: keep the stable part first on every retry, reuse matching chunks, keep the slot between runs, and pre-warm role prompts when disk allows.
lessons.evidence: [M] retry templates keep the stable part first (arch_selftest_promptprefix); llama prefix reuse reported as cache_n. Not yet measured as seconds saved per run: verify_machine --gpu steps 'prefix reuse cache_n/prompt_n' and 'slot save -> restore'.

lessons.lesson: Speculation is the cheapest speed: n-gram by default, a static lookup built from the project's own names as an opt-in, a draft only with the worker's exact tokenizer.
lessons.evidence: [M] n-gram speculation on edits 56 -> 306-343 tok/s; the project lookup on top is community practice, not yet measured here (verify_machine --gpu 'n-gram speculation on vs off').

lessons.lesson: Read prompts in sane chunks (ubatch 128-1024, batch >= ubatch) and run decode threads on the performance cores only (-t), prompt threads on all cores (-tb).
lessons.evidence: [M] machine audit 2026-11-03: 11 threads on a 4 P-core + 4 E-core laptop was worse than the performance cores; batch sizes are [B] llama.cpp docs, sweet spot on this card not yet measured.

lessons.lesson: A mixture-of-experts model whose experts live in RAM is pinned (mlock) and read whole (no-mmap), its cache is q4_0 beside the worker, and it stays loaded so switching costs about a second.
lessons.evidence: [M] heavy beside the worker 14-16 tok/s with switching in about 1 s; a load of the 13 GB model was 24 s. q4_0 cache and mlock/no-mmap are [B] llama.cpp docs; their own gain is not yet measured here.

lessons.lesson: Ollama holds a model for about a minute after a call, not ten: a heavy MoE held in RAM is ~20 GB and the resident servers need that room.
lessons.evidence: [M] Ollama had put 28% of the heavy MoE on the card and the worker got 9 of 36 layers (7.96 tok/s vs 55 for the 8B); Ollama default holds a model for minutes.

lessons.lesson: The fast lane gives the worker the whole card, so the heavy model is no longer resident: choose it for worker-only work; when most runs plan, keep the heavy model beside the worker instead.
lessons.evidence: [M] restart cost 5-8 s per heavy load; fast-lane window arithmetic proven in arch_selftest_fastlane. The net gain per run depends on how often the planner runs; compare with and without on this machine.

lessons.lesson: Work that needs no model should cost nothing twice: tool results cached inside a run, file ranking remembered, the index updated incrementally, earlier agents handed as digests.
lessons.evidence: [M] 8-finding result of ~5,000 characters reaches the next phase as <= 800; rank cache and incremental index re-read only files whose size or time changed (arch_selftest_cacheplus).

lessons.lesson: When Claude is allowed, make its bill small by structure: a shared prefix first, the cache lifetime chosen by use (auto), read-only agents on the cheaper model, non-urgent work through the batch API at half price.
lessons.evidence: [M] Claude lead 98% prompt-cache hit with the shared header; a 6-call Council answer fell from $0.27 to $0.18. A 1-hour cache write costs 2x a 5-minute one (1.25x), [B] pricing. No live Claude call is made by the tests.

lessons.lesson: An agent that runs more than once per run belongs on the worker: on a 6 GB card a heavy verifier is a model swap on every call. The planner runs once and stays heavy.
lessons.evidence: [M] a heavy load costs 5-15 s here (24 s cold for the 13 GB MoE); shipped workflows run the verifier up to 3x (panels). The verifier's pass/fail quality on the worker vs heavy is not yet measured: compare with `swap --trial`.

lessons.lesson: A near-duplicate request on an unchanged project reuses the last validated plan and its context files; the gates still run, and any change to a file the plan depends on drops the entry.
lessons.evidence: Design rule (Jaccard >= 0.8 and the same touched files); proven by arch_selftest_reqcache. Hit rate on real use is not measured yet (arch_reqcache.stats()).

lessons.lesson: A newly downloaded model gets a passport, a family and a plan for every job, written as a suggestion; nothing is applied until a trial passes.
lessons.evidence: Rule from the swap work: scores are estimates until n >= 8 tasks are measured; apply refuses without a passed trial in the last 7 days.

lessons.lesson: A 7B-8B model that stays 100% on the GPU outperforms a 14B model that spills >30% of its weights to system RAM: penalize CPU-spill in role scoring and cap unified-memory heavy selection at 70% of RAM.
lessons.evidence: [M] 14B spilling 59% to DDR4 ran at 6-9 tok/s vs 55-70 tok/s for 100% GPU-resident 8B; score_for_role applies a split penalty when gpu_ratio < 0.7 and arch_server.plan subtracts live Ollama VRAM from desktop_gb.

lessons.lesson: Enable Flash Attention and q8_0 KV cache quantization on both llama-server and Ollama so 8k-16k contexts use half the VRAM without displacing model layers.
lessons.evidence: [M] fp16 KV cache at 8k-16k consumed 1.5-2.2 GB on 6 GB cards; q8_0 KV + Flash Attention halves KV memory on both llama-server (-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on) and Ollama (OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1, OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0).

lessons.lesson: A writer agent's step-cache key must hash both its owned files and the rest of the repository (deps_hash), and test reuse must hash non-source data fixtures too.
lessons.evidence: Without deps_hash, a cached writer step replayed stale code after a shared helper changed; files_fingerprint(exclude=owns) and _tree_hash now hash all non-ignored project files.

lessons.lesson: Distributed LAN hosts must rank by queue-aware effective speed tok_s / (1 + in_flight), cap per-host concurrency, support both Ollama and llama-server (/v1/models), and fail over to the local machine mid-run on network errors.
lessons.evidence: Unbounded fan-out to one LAN rig caused head-of-line timeouts, and Crew._loop previously rejected remote role_hosts; rank_hosts, _IN_FLIGHT, and mark_down now route and fail over cleanly.

lessons.lesson: Show non-technical stakeholders both the $0 local inference bill against cloud API equivalents (Opus, Sonnet, GPT-4o, seat plans) and the 10 active optimization layers, backed by a one-click visual frontend demo.
lessons.evidence: Built arch_finops.report, markdown_report, and create_visual_demo (/api/arch/finops, /api/arch/demo, Models > Speed > FinOps & savings) with zero cloud calls.

lessons.lesson: Switching between Antigravity, Claude Code, and local models must never introduce placeholder stubs, shrink existing modules, or weaken a gate: DEF: merges, the shrink guard, and arch_fakecode.py block every stub.
lessons.evidence: Whole-file rewrites and naive agent edits can drop functions or leave pass/TODO stubs; core.replace_def, core.merge_partial, and arch_fakecode.scan enforce real implementations across all platforms.
